NASHR:v1p447/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p447/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p447/r1.claim: The hamza image is omitted from riʾyan to avoid two identical y-shaped letters; Ibn al-Jazari rejects the explanation that the kasra alone makes its image unnecessary.
NASHR:v1p447/r1.anchor: والصواب أن ذلك كراهة اجتماع المثلين؛ لأنها لو صورت لكانت ياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r14.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r14.claim: Abū ʿAlī treats al-rayy as the verbal noun of being watered and also as a passive participle meaning watered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r14.anchor: الري: مصدر رويت من الماء، واسم مفعول أي مروي قاله أبو علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r15.claim: Al-zī means collected beauties and derives from gathering.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r15.anchor: الزي: محاسن مجموعة من الزي وهو الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r3.claim: God destroyed many generations who had better worldly circumstances to warn the taunting unbelievers that He can destroy them too, and to prompt reflection; fine possessions and refreshment did not save deniers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى كثرة ما أهلك من القرون ممن كان أحسن حالا منهم في الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r4.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r4.claim: They parse 'they are better' as an adjective of kam, which requires placing the adjective in the accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وهم أحسن في محل النصب صفة لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r5.claim: The author says interrogative or exclamatory kam is neither modified nor a modifier in Basran grammar; hum ahsan instead modifies qarn, pluralized because a generation contains many individuals, though singular agreement would also be Arabic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r5.anchor: ونص أصحابنا على أن كم الاستفهامية والخبرية لا توصف ولا يوصف بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r6.claim: The interpretation of athāth has already been discussed in Sūrat al-Naḥl.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r6.anchor: وتقدم تفسير الأثاث في سورة النحل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r7.claim: The majority read riʾyan with hamza, a form of vision meaning something seen, like grinding and watering as verbal nouns with passive force.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ورءيا بالهمزة من رؤية العين فعل بمعنى مفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains al-riʾy as appearance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r9.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r9.claim: Al-Hasan interprets it as forms or figures.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r10.speaker: الزهري وأبو جعفر وشيبة وطلحة وأيوب وابن سعدان وابن ذكوان وقالون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r10.claim: They read riyyan with a doubled yāʾ and no hamza; it may derive from hamzated rawāʾ ('appearance'), with hamza eased and the two yāʾs assimilated, or from rayy ('well-watered'), evoking freshness and beauty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p290/r10.anchor: بتشديد الياء من غير همز، فاحتمل أن يكون مهموز الأصل من الرواء والمنظر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Arabic word qarn can mean either the people of one era or a nation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The word Q refers to “people of one era” as well as to a “nation.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Material wealth, resources, and splendour do not indicate divine favour or protect a nation from God’s grasp; destroyed earlier peoples demonstrate this.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: things save it from God’s grasp. The fate of previous nations bears witness to this

BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r1.claim: Qarn is explained by min qarn; each age's people are a generation for those after them, and Kashifi defines a qarn as a group gathered in one time.
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r1.anchor: كم فعول أهلكنا ومن قرن بيان لإبهامها وأهل كل عصر قرن لمن بعدهم

BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r2.claim: Athath means household furniture; r'ya means outward appearance and derives from seeing.
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r2.anchor: تمييز عن النسبة وهو متاع البيت يعني

BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r3.claim: Earlier peoples including ʿAd and Thamud had more worldly goods and appearance than Quraysh yet were destroyed, showing bounty did not mark divine favor and warning Quraysh.
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r3.anchor: كثيرا من القرون التي كانوا أفضل منهم فيما يفتخرون به من الحظوظ الدنيوية كعاد وثمود

BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r4.claim: Al-Kashifi's couplet says neither wealth nor beauty saved earlier peoples from destruction and punishment.
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (نه آن مال هلاك از ايشان دفع كرد ونه آن جمال عذاب

BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r5.claim: The inward reading contrasts seekers who discipline and humble themselves with deniers who indulge in wealth, pride, and desire; earlier nations were destroyed by love of the world and status.
BURSEVI:v5p270#2/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن أهل الإنكار وأهل العزة بالله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r1.claim: Earlier peoples such as ʿĀd and Thamud had greater worldly comforts yet were destroyed; prosperity does not prove divine favor, and the verse threatens the boasters.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r1.anchor: فلو دل حصول نعمة الدنيا للانسان على كونه مكرم عند الله تعالى وجب أن لا يهلك أحد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r2.claim: كم is most naturally an exclamatory or informative expression of abundance, fronted as its syntax requires; an interrogative reading is also reported.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r2.anchor: خبرية للتكثير مفعول ( أهلكنا ) وقدمت لصدارتها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r3.claim: A generation is the people of an age; its duration is disputed, and the word derives from a horn because it projects or precedes.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r3.anchor: والقرن أهل كل عصرا وقد اختلف في مدته وهو من قرن الدابة سمى به لتقدمة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r4.claim: They parse “better in furnishings and appearance” as an accusative adjective qualifying كم.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r4.anchor: هم احسن في حيز النصب على ما ذهب اليه الزمخشري وتبعه أبو البقاء صفه لكم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r5.claim: He objects that كم, whether informative or interrogative, is not modified by an adjective, and instead attaches the description to قرن.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r5.anchor: لا توصف ولا يوصف بها وجعله صفة ( قرن )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r6.claim: The plural pronoun is grammatical because a generation comprises many individuals; singular agreement would also be Arabic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r6.anchor: وضمير الجمع لاشتمال القرن على أفراد كثيرة ولو افرد الضمير لكان عربيا ايضا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r7.claim: اثاث is the household goods that furnish a home, including carpets and clothing; some deny a singular, while another distinction contrasts new furnishings with worn goods.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r7.anchor: واحدها اثاثة وقيل : لا واحد لها وقيل : الاثاث ما جد من المتاع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r8.speaker: الحسن بن علي الطوسي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r8.claim: A verse illustrates furnishings becoming worn through age, supporting the distinction between اثاث and خرثى.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r8.anchor: تقادم العهد من أم الوليد بنا دهرا وصارا اثاث البيت خريثا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r9.claim: رئيا means outward appearance; it is a verbal noun used in the sense of a seen object.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r9.anchor: والرئى المنظر كما قال ابن عباس وغيره وهو فعل بمعنى مفعول من الرؤية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r10.speaker: الزهري وأبو جعفر وشيبة وطلحة وأيوب وابن سعدان وابن ذكوان وقالون
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r10.claim: They read ريا with a doubled yā and no hamza; it can derive from رؤيا by changing and assimilating the hamza, or from luxuriance and freshness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r10.anchor: ابن سعدان وابن ذكوان وقالون ريا بتشديد الياء من غير همز

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r11.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r11.claim: One reading has رَيْئًا with a still yā followed by hamza; it reflects metathesis and has the pattern فلعا.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r11.anchor: في رواية الأعمش ( ريئا ) بياء ساكنة بعدها همزة وهو على القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r12.speaker: اليزيدي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r12.claim: A reading رياء is explained as mutual display among people.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r12.anchor: بياء بعدها الف بعدها همزة حكاها اليزيد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r13.claim: His shortened reading ريا is not erroneous: it can simplify a doubled yā or move the hamza's vowel and then delete it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r13.anchor: بحذف الهمزة والوقصر وتجاسر بعض الناس وقال : هي لحن وليس كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير ويزيد البربري والأعصم المكي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r14.claim: They read زيا, meaning gathered beauties or adornments; the source says the verse's apparent meaning remains furnishings and appearance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r14.anchor: بالزاى وتشديد الياء وهو المحاسن المجموعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r15.speaker: الثقافي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r15.claim: A poem uses زي for attractive furnishings, evidence for the reading's sense of gathered adornment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p125#2/r15.anchor: اشاقتك الظعائن يوم بانوا بذي الزي الجميل من الاثاث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r5.claim: God answers their boast by recalling past generations who were destroyed despite having better furnishings, possessions, and wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r5.anchor: {وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا} أي متاعا وأموالا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r6.claim: Muqatil explains the generations' superior furnishings as better clothes.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r7.speaker: أكثر القراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r7.claim: Most readers pronounce رئيا with hamza, meaning appearance or what is seen.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r7.anchor: أكثر القراء بالهمز أي: منظرا من "الرؤية"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r8.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر ونافع غير ورش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r8.claim: These readers pronounce it riyyā without hamza: either the same word with hamza removed or luxuriant prosperity that appears in one's looks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p252#2/r8.anchor: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر ونافع غير ورش: "وريا" مشددا بغير همز

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:74/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:74/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:74/r1.claim: “How many” is the object of “destroyed,” and “generations” explains it; a generation is named for the animal’s leading horn. Household goods are furnishings, perhaps specifically new possessions; appearance derives from seeing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:74/r1.anchor: وإنما سمي أهل كل عصر قرنا أي مقدما من قرن الدابة

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:74/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:74/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:74/r2.claim: Readings change, invert, or omit the hamza, or give “zayyā,” a collection of beauties; worldly enjoyment is entrapment rather than honor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:74/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر «ريا» على قلب الهمزة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p553/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p553/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p553/r1.claim: The unprefixed before signals that all earlier generations enjoyed better circumstances; the audience saw their homes and traces, and they had finer furnishings and appearance.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p553/r1.anchor: لم يأت بالجار إعلاما بأن المتقدمين كلهم كانوا أرغد عيشا وأمكن حالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r4.claim: God addresses the Prophet with an intervening reminder that many earlier generations enjoyed greater furnishings and more beautiful appearance than the Arab polytheists; this threatens them before the answer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r4.anchor: وقد أهلك الله أهل قرون كثيرة كانوا أرفه من مشركي العرب متاعا وأجمل منهم منظرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r5.claim: Athāth means household furnishings used for adornment; the majority read rʾyan with hamza as a passive form meaning visible appearance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r5.anchor: والأثاث : متاع البيوت الذي يتزين به ، و { رئيا } قرأه الجمهور بهمزة بعد الراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r6.speaker: قالون عن نافع، وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r6.claim: These readers use riyyan without hamza, either by turning the hamza into yāʾ and assimilating it, or deriving it from luxuriant, well-watered ease.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p154/r6.anchor: وقرأه قالون عن نافع وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر ( ريا ) بتشديد الياء بلا همزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.claim: The rhetorical “how many” breaks their boast: God destroyed earlier peoples with greater strength, wealth, and beauty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.anchor: هذا الذي افتخروا به لا قدر له عند الله وليس بمنج لهم فكم أهلك الله من الأمم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.claim: A qarn is a nation of one era; estimates differ between one hundred, eighty, and seventy years.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.anchor: واختلف الناس في قدر المدة التي إذا اجتمعت لأمة سميت تلك الأمة قرنا، فقيل مائة سنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.claim: Athāth broadly covers property, goods, and livestock; scholars disagree whether it is singular or plural.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.anchor: و «الأثاث» المال العين والعرض والحيوان وهو اسم عام واختلف هل هو جمع أو إفراد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says athāth is a collective noun with no singular of the same form, like matāʿ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r1.anchor: فقال الفراء: هو اسم جمع لا واحد له من لفظه كالمتاع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r2.speaker: خلف الأحمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r2.claim: Khalaf al-Aḥmar says athāth is a plural whose singular is athātha, like ḥamāma and ḥamām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r2.anchor: وقال خلف الأحمر: هو جمع واحده أثاثة كحمامة وحمام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r3.speaker: أبو العباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās cites a poem using athāth for possessions or furnishings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r3.anchor: وأنشد أبو العباس: [الوافر] لقد علمت عرينة حيث كانت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r4.speaker: نافع وأهل المدينة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ in one transmission and the people of Medina read riyyan with a geminated yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع بخلاف وأهل المدينة «وريا» بياء مشددة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وطلحة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās in one report and Ṭalḥa read riyyan with a light yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس فيما روي عنه وطلحة «وريا» بياء مخففة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r6.claim: These readers use hamza followed by yāʾ; Ibn ʿAbbās explains the word as appearance and al-Ḥasan as forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي «ورءيا» بهمزة بعدها ياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r7.speaker: أشهب عن نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r7.claim: Ashhab transmits the hamzated reading from Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r7.anchor: ورويت عن نافع وابن عامر رواها أشهب عن نافع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r8.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r8.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads riyʾan with a quiescent yāʾ before hamza, an inversion traced to raʾā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم «وريئا» بياء ساكنة بعدها همزة وهو على القلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r9.claim: One analysis equates the geminated-yāʾ reading with the hamzated one, softening hamza to match verse endings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r9.anchor: فقيل هي بمعنى المهموزة إلا أن الهمزة خففت لتستوي رؤوس الآي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r10.speaker: منذر بن سعيد عن بعض أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r10.claim: A view reported by Mundhir ibn Saʿīd derives the word from irrigation: their lands were better watered and more abundant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r10.anchor: وذكر منذر بن سعيد عن بعض أهل العلم أنه من «الري» في السقي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r11.claim: The light-yāʾ reading has a weak analysis; some even call it erroneous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r11.anchor: وأما القراءة المخففة الياء فضعيفة الوجه، وقد قيل هي لحن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ويزيد البربري وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r12.claim: These readers also read zayyan, meaning clothing or outward appearance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p28#3/r12.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير ويزيد البربري وابن عباس أيضا «وزيا» بالزاي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p258/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p258/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p258/r1.claim: The destruction of earlier generations is cross-referenced to al-Anʿam 6:6, and the explanation of furnishings to al-Naḥl 16:80.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p258/r1.anchor: وقد بينا معنى القرن في الأنعام 6 وشرحنا الاثاث في النحل 80

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r2.claim: God refutes their boast by recalling many destroyed communities who had better furnishings, wealth, belongings, and appearances.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257/r2.anchor: أي: وكم من أمة وقرن من المكذبين قد أهلكناهم بكفرهم، {هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257#2/r1.claim: Reports define athath as wealth, furnishings, or clothing, while r'iy means appearance; Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and others support the latter gloss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257#2/r1.anchor: ومنهم من قال في الأثاث: هو المال. ومنهم من قال: المتاع. ومنهم من قال: الثياب، والرئي: المنظر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257#2/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says r'iy means forms; Malik says the phrase means greater wealth and better appearance, and Ibn Kathir considers these explanations compatible and sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p257#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: يعني الصور، وكذا قال مالك: {أثاثا ورئيا} : أكثر أموالا وأحسن صورا

JISHUMI:v6p4597/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r9.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r9.claim: Athāth is household goods such as furniture and clothing; al-Aṣamm gives it a singular form.
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r9.anchor: واحدها: أثاثة، كحمام وحمامة، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v6p4597/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r10.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says athāth has no singular and gives alternative plural forms.

JISHUMI:v6p4597/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r11.claim: Raʾy is the visible outward condition seen in a group; the noun names what is seen.
JISHUMI:v6p4597/r11.anchor: والرئي: ما يراه الرجل من ظاهر أحوال القوم

JISHUMI:v6p4600/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r10.claim: Athāth is worldly possessions and adornment; raʾyan may mean appearance.
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r10.anchor: ورئيا قيل: هيئة، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v6p4600/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r11.speaker: الأصم وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r11.anchor: وقيل: منظرا حسنا، عن الأصم، وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v6p4600/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r12.claim: As wealth could not save earlier generations from destruction, it cannot save these unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v6p4600/r12.anchor: كما لم يغن عنهم مالهم عند إهلاكهم كذلك لا يغني عن هؤلاء

JISHUMI:v6p4603/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4603/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4603/r10.claim: Worldly wealth and leadership cannot benefit a person at the Resurrection, as destroyed nations show.
JISHUMI:v6p4603/r10.anchor: وتدل على أن المال والرئاسة في الدنيا لا يغني عنه شيئا يوم القيامة

AKHFASH:v2p440/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p440/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p440/r1.claim: رئيا derives from seeing and is glossed as appearance, confirming derivation from رأيت.
AKHFASH:v2p440/r1.anchor: وقال {ورءيا} ف"الرءي" من الرؤية وفسروه من المنظر فذاك يدل علىأنه من "رأيت".

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r1.claim: The phrase “how many generations” is the object of أهلكنا, with “of generations” clarifying its ambiguity; each age is a generation relative to those after it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r1.anchor: تبيين لإبهامها ، أي : كثيرا من القرون أهلكنا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r2.claim: “They were better” is an accusative adjective describing كم; without the pronoun phrase, أحسن itself would need accusative adjective inflection.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r3.claim: Athāth means household furnishings; another view restricts it to fine bedding, while khirthī means worn furnishings or garments.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r3.anchor: متاع البيت . وقيل : هو ماجد من الفرش

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Ṭūsī's poem uses athāth for household goods that have become worn, witnessing the contrast with khirthī.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r5.claim: The readings of رئيا include “appearance/form,” an inverted form, hamza-to-yāʾ with assimilation, and derivation from luxury and blessing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r5.anchor: وهو المنظر والهيئة فعل بمعنى مفعول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r6.claim: Further readings drop the hamza after shifting it, or read زيا from collected adornments; all mean the earlier generations looked better.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p38/r6.anchor: وهو الجمع ؛ لأن الزي محاسن مجموعة

FARRA:v2p170/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p170/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p170/r8.claim: Athāth means household goods and has no singular, like matāʿ; Arabs use several plurals for matāʿ, while athāth has forms ātha and athat.
FARRA:v2p170/r8.anchor: وقوله: أحسن أثاثا ورءيا [74] الأثاث: المتاع. والرئي: المنظر، والأثاث لا واحد له

FARRA:v2p170/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p170/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p170/r9.claim: Medinan readers pronounce riy without hamza, a good reading in context; some derive riʾy from seeing, while others read ziy for appearance or attire.
FARRA:v2p170/r9.anchor: وأهل المدينة يقرءونها بغير همز (وريا) وهو وجه جيد

FARRA:v2p170/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p170/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p170/r10.claim: Zayy means appearance or style; Arabs say zayyaytu al-jāriya when they dress and adorn her.
FARRA:v2p170/r10.anchor: وقد قرأ بعضهم (وزيا) بالزاي. والزي: الهيئة والمنظر. والعرب تقول: قد زييت الجارية

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r3.claim: Athath means household goods and riy means appearance or visible display.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r3.anchor: أن الأثاث : المتاع , والرئي : المنظر , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r4.claim: Further meanings are new household clothing and enjoying blessings, unseen versus visible possessions, greater wealth and better appearance, or useful goods versus ornaments; a poet illustrates riy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p385/r4.anchor: أن الأثاث ما كان جديدا من ثياب البيت , والرئي الارتواء من النعمة

MUJAHID:v1p390/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p390/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p390/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses athathan as adornment or furnishings.
MUJAHID:v1p390/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله أثاثا قال يعني الزينة

MUJAHID:v1p390/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p390/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p390/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses r'iyan as what people see outwardly.

MUQATIL:19:73-74/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r3.claim: A qarn is a nation; God destroyed earlier nations with softer furnishings and a better appearance than Mecca's people, destroying their wealth and bodies.
MUQATIL:19:73-74/r3.anchor: قبل أهل مكة، { من قرن } ، يعني أمة، كقوله عز وجل:

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r1.claim: كم is the object of أهلكنا; من explains its ambiguity, and a generation is each era's people in relation to those after it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r1.anchor: كم مفعول أهلكنا ومن تبيين لابهامها أي كثيرا من القرون أهلكنا وكل أهل عصر قرن لمن بعدهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r2.claim: من قرن is in the accusative as an adjective of كم; without من, قرنا would be a clearer accusative adjective.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r2.anchor: في محل النصب صفة لكم ألا ترى أنك لو تركتهم كان أحسن نصبا على الوصفية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r3.claim: أثاث means household goods, or the newest furnishings and carpets.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r3.anchor: هو متاع البيت أو ماجد من الفرش

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r4.claim: رئيا means appearance and aspect and is on the passive participle pattern from seeing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r4.anchor: منظرا وهيئة فعل بمعنى مفعول من رأيت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r5.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r5.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read ريا without hamza and with doubled yā, either by changing the hamza to yā and assimilating it or from الري, blessing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p45#2/r5.anchor: وريا بغير همز مشددا نافع وابن عامر على قلب الهمزة ياء لسكونها وانكسار ما قبلها ثم الادغام أو من الري الذي هو النعمة

MAJAZ:v2p9/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p9/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p9/r6.claim: أثاثا means belongings or furnishings, specifically good belongings.

MAJAZ:v2p9/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p9/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p9/r7.claim: ورءيا is outward appearance, what is visible about a person.
MAJAZ:v2p9/r7.anchor: «ورءيا» (74) وهو ما ظهر عليه ورأيته عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r2.claim: “Qarn” means a nation or community; earlier generations had abundant possessions and “athāth” means household goods.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r2.anchor: أي من أمة وجماعة. { هم أحسن أثاثا } أي متاعا كثيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r3.claim: One explanation distinguishes new furnishings, “athāth,” from used household goods, “kharathī”; a verse by al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Ṭūsī illustrates the latter.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو ما جد من الفرش والخرثي ما لبس منها

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “athāth” as appearance and Muqātil as clothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هيئة. مقاتل: ثيابا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r5.claim: “Riya” means a fine appearance; five readings are listed, including Medinan unhamzated, Kufan hamzated, Ṭalḥa’s softened form, Ibn ʿAbbās’s zāy form, and an alternative hamzated form.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r5.anchor: وفيه خمس قراءات: قرأ أهل المدينة «وريا» بغير همز

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r6.speaker: أهل المدينة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r6.claim: Their unhamzated reading may derive from “raʾaytu,” with hamza softened into yāʾ and the yāʾs merged, fitting the rhyme and meaning good appearance and clothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r6.anchor: أن تكون من رأيت ثم خففت الهمزة فأبدل منها ياء

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “al-raʾy” as appearance, yielding the sense that they had finer furnishings and clothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الرئي المنظر فالمعنى: هم أحسن أثاثا ولباسا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r8.claim: A second explanation of the unhamzated form derives it from well-watered skin from worldly blessing.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r9.speaker: ورش عن نافع وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r9.claim: These transmitters read “warʾiyyan” with hamza, as do the Kufans and Abū ʿAmr, following the original form from “raʾaytu.”
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r9.anchor: وفي رواية ورش عن نافع وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر «ورئيا» بالهمز

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r10.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r10.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif reads the word with one softened yāʾ; al-Qurṭubī suspects this is an error.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r10.anchor: وقراءة طلحة بن مصرف «وريا» بياء واحدة مخففة أحسبها غلطا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r11.speaker: بعض النحويين
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r11.claim: Some grammarians derive the form from an original hamza changed to yāʾ, then delete one of the two yāʾs.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r11.anchor: وقد زعم بعض النحويين أنه كان أصلها الهمز فقلبت الهمزة ياء

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r12.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r12.claim: Al-Mahdawī proposes “riʾan” becoming “riyyan,” followed by transfer of the hamza’s vowel and its deletion.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r12.anchor: المهدوي: ويجوز أن يكون «ريئا» فقلبت ياء فصارت رييا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r13.claim: Another reading uses metathesis to produce “riya”; Sibawayh records “rāʾ” as a form meaning “he saw.”
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r13.anchor: وقد قرأ بعضهم «وريا» على القلب وهي القراءة الخامسة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r14.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r14.claim: Al-Jawharī says the hamzated form means visible beauty and conspicuous dress; Abū ʿUbayda cites a line by Muḥammad ibn Numayr al-Thaqafī as evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:74/r14.anchor: من همزه جعله من المنظر من رأيت، وهو ما رأته العين

QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r1.claim: The unhamzated reading may reflect hamza-softening or derive from healthy coloring; Ibn ʿAbbās, Ubayy, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and others read “ziyan,” meaning good bearing or beauty.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r1.anchor: ومن لم يهمز إما أن يكون على تخفيف الهمزة أو يكون من رويت ألوانهم

QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وسعيد بن جبير والأعسم المكي ويزيد البربري
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r2.claim: These authorities read “ziyan” with zāy, meaning bearing and beauty; it may derive from “zawaytu,” gathered, with wāw changed to yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r2.anchor: قراءة ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وسعيد بن جبير والأعسم المكي ويزيد البربري «وزيا» بالزاي

QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r3.claim: The Prophet’s expression “the earth was gathered for me” illustrates the root meaning “gathered.”

QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r4.claim: The former peoples’ fine possessions did not avert death or God’s punishment, whether through later punishment or punishment in this life.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:75/r4.anchor: أي فلم يغن ذلك عنهم شيئا من عذاب الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r1.claim: Earlier peoples enjoyed even greater worldly blessings yet God destroyed them; this disproves either that worldly prosperity proves divine favor or that God's beloved cannot suffer worldly grief.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r1.anchor: إن من كان أعظم نعمة منكم في الدنيا قد أهلكهم الله تعالى وأبادهم

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r2.claim: A generation is a people of an age in relation to those who come after, because they precede them; أحسن is accusative as an adjective of كم.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r2.anchor: أهل كل عصر قرن لمن بعدهم لأنهم يتقدمونهم وهم أحسن في محل النصب صفة لكم

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r4.claim: One r-āʾ reading with a silent hamza followed by yāʾ means appearance or form, on the pattern of a passive participle from رأيت.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r4.anchor: بهمزة ساكنة بعدها ياء وهو المنظر والهيئة فعل بمعنى مفعول من رأيت رئيا

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r5.claim: Another r-āʾ reading, ريئا, has metathesis, like راء from رأى.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r5.anchor: ريئا على القلب كقولهم راء في رأى

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r6.claim: A doubled-yāʾ r-āʾ reading comes from changing hamza to yāʾ and assimilating, or from الري meaning luxury and well-being.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r6.anchor: بالياء المشددة على قلب الهمزة ياء ، والإدغام

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r7.claim: A further yāʾ reading deletes hamza from ريئا and transfers its vowel to the preceding quiescent yāʾ.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r7.anchor: بالياء على حذف الهمزة رأسا ووجهه أن يخفف المقلوب

RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r8.claim: The zāy reading زيا derives from zayy, a collection of adornments; the phrase then means they looked better than these people.
RAZI-FULL:v21p210#4/r8.anchor: وأما بالزاي المنقطة من فوق زيا فاشتقاقه من الزي

STUDYQURAN:19:74/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:74/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:74/r1.claim: The recurring destruction of earlier generations warns Quraysh that material wealth and status cannot protect wrongdoers from punishment; those earlier peoples had more than the Makkans yet were destroyed.
STUDYQURAN:19:74/r1.anchor: were destroyed for their wrongdoing, despite having a better earthly provision and material situation than the Makkans

STUDYQURAN:19:74/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:74/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:74/r2.claim: This answers the disbelievers' claim in the previous verse that they surpassed believers in station and company.
STUDYQURAN:19:74/r2.anchor: a response to the implicit claim of the disbelievers in v. 73

NAHHAS:v3p25/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p25/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p25/r8.claim: Five readings: Madinans وريا without hamza; Kufans and Abū ʿAmr ورئيا; Ṭalḥa light single yāʾ; Ibn ʿAbbās وزيا with zāy; Abū Isḥāq allows ورئيا with yāʾ then hamza.
NAHHAS:v3p25/r8.anchor: فيه خمس قراءات قرأ أهل المدينة ( وريا ) بغير همز

NAHHAS:v3p25/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p25/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p25/r9.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls the Madinan reading good: it may derive from رأيت with softened hamza assimilated to yāʾ and harmonize with unhamzated verse endings.
NAHHAS:v3p25/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر قراءة أهل المدينة في هذا حسنة وفيها تقديران

NAHHAS:v3p25/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p25/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p25/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets الري as appearance, so the people are better in furnishings and clothing.
NAHHAS:v3p25/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا قال ابن عباس الري المنظر والمعنى هم أحسن أثاثا

NAHHAS:v3p25/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p25/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p25/r11.claim: A second analysis derives ريا from being watered and means the skin is replete with blessing; as a verbal noun it has no hamza.
NAHHAS:v3p25/r11.anchor: والوجه الثاني أن يكون المعنى أن جلودهم مرتوية من النعمة

NAHHAS:v3p25/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p25/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p25/r12.claim: Kufans and Abū ʿAmr preserve the hamza from رأيت; Ṭalḥa's light single yāʾ seems mistaken, though some explain it by dropping hamza.
NAHHAS:v3p25/r12.anchor: وقراءة أهل الكوفة وأبي عمرو من رأيت على الأصل

NAHHAS:v3p25/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p25/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p25/r13.claim: The zāy reading means appearance or bearing; the fifth form reflects hamza metathesis, as Sībawayh attests راء for رأى.
NAHHAS:v3p25/r13.anchor: والزي الهيأة والقراءة الخامسة على قلب الهمزة حكى سيبويه

TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r1.claim: Earlier generations had more household goods and better appearances than the boastful unbelievers, yet God destroyed their property and changed their appearance.
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r1.anchor: وأحسن منهم منظرا وأجمل صورا، فأهلكنا أموالهم، وغيرنا صورهم،

TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses athāth as household goods and raʾy as appearance.
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {أحسن أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] قال: الرئي: المنظر، والأثاث: المتاع

TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r3.claim: In another report Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the terms as wealth and appearance.
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أحسن أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] الأثاث: المال، والرئي: المنظر

TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses athāth as fine furnishings and raʾy as wealth.
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله {أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] قال: الأثاث: أحسن المتاع، والرئي: قال: المال

TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says the earlier people had more possessions, a better standing and residence; God destroyed their wealth and disfigured them.
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، يقول الله تبارك وتعالى: {وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] أي أكثر متاعا وأحسن منزلة ومستقرا،

TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid glosses athāth as goods and raʾy as what people see.
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أثاثا} [النحل: 80] قال: المتاع {ورئيا} [مريم: 74] قال: فيما يرى الناس

TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r7.claim: Alqama's verse uses raʾy for the visible appearance or display of goods; ṣawwān is a chest where clothes are kept.
TAB-FULL:v15p610#2/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك قول علقمة بن عبدة: [البحر الطويل] كميت كلون الأرجوان نشرته

TAB-FULL:v15p612/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses raʾy as a handsome appearance and athāth as wealth.
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: الأثاث: المال، والرئي: المنظر الحسن

TAB-FULL:v15p612/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes raʾy as appearance in color and beauty.
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ورئيا} [مريم: 74] منظرا في اللون والحسن

TAB-FULL:v15p612/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says athāth means household goods and raʾy means appearance.
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {أحسن أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] قال: الرئي: المنظر، والأثاث: المتاع،

TAB-FULL:v15p612/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r4.claim: Most Medinan readers read riyyan without hamza, either replacing hamza with yāʾ and merging the yāʾs, or deriving it from rawiya to mean good judgment about one's property.
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r4.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء أهل المدينة: (وريا) غير مهموز، وذلك إذا قرئ كذلك يتوجه لوجهين:

TAB-FULL:v15p612/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r5.claim: Most Iraqi readers pronounce the hamza, taking the word to mean visual appearance.
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r5.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء العراق والكوفة والبصرة {ورئيا} [مريم: 74] بهمزها، بمعنى: رؤية العين،

TAB-FULL:v15p612/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r6.claim: A reported reading with zāy means finer possessions, adornment, and appearance, from the word for adornment and form.
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r6.anchor: وحكي عن بعضهم أنه قرأ: (أحسن أثاثا وزيا) بالزاي، كأنه أراد أحسن متاعا وهيئة ومنظرا،

TAB-FULL:v15p612/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r7.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the hamzated reading because the interpreters agree on visual appearance, which derives from sight; he accepts the unhamzated reading with that meaning too.
TAB-FULL:v15p612/r7.anchor: وأولى القراءات في ذلك بالصواب، قراءة من قرأ {أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] بالراء والهمز، لإجماع الحجة

TAB-FULL:v15p614/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r1.speaker: الأحمر
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r1.claim: Al-Aḥmar says athāth is a collective plural whose singular is athātha, like ḥamām and saḥāb.
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r1.anchor: فكان الأحمر فيما ذكر لي عنه يقول: هو جمع، واحدتها أثاثة، كما الحمام جمع واحدتها حمامة.

TAB-FULL:v15p614/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r2.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says athāth has no singular, like matāʿ; he proposes forms if it were pluralized, and says the plural of raʾy is ārāʾ.
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r2.anchor: وأما الفراء فإنه كان يقول: لا واحد له، كما أن المتاع لا واحد له.

TAB-FULL:v15p614/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r3.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the zāy reading because it departs from the reciters' reading, even though its interpretation is sound.
TAB-FULL:v15p614/r3.anchor: وأما قراءته بالزاي فقراءة خارجة، عن قراءة القراء، فلا أستجيز القراءة بها

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r6.claim: Qarn denotes people living together in one period, and athāth denotes household furnishings.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r6.anchor: القرن الناس المقترنون في زمن واحد، والأثاث متاع البيت

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r7.claim: Some lexicographers say athāth is used only for a large quantity and has no singular form from the same root.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r7.anchor: قيل لا يطلق إلا على الكثير ولا واحد له من لفظه

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r8.claim: A report in al-Majmaʿ says raʾy here means visible appearance, not the verbal noun; raʾy is the act of seeing and raʾy is what is seen.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r8.anchor: نقل في مجمع البيان عن بعضهم أنه اسم لما ظهر وليس بالمصدر وإنما المصدر الرأي والرؤية

TABATABAI:19:74-75/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r9.claim: The disbelievers overlook human life after death, which is everlasting; a few worldly days count for little against eternity and cannot secure happiness.
TABATABAI:19:74-75/r9.anchor: أن للإنسان حياة خالدة أبدية لا منتهى لها وإنما سعادته في سعادتها والأيام القلائل التي يعيش فيها في الدنيا لا قدر لها قبال ما لا نهاية له

TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r1.claim: Worldly pleasures neither guarantee happiness nor protect people from divine anger; a life threatened by destruction is no secure blessing.
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r1.anchor: هذه التمتعات الدنيوية لا تحتم له السعادة ولا تقيه من غضب الله إن حل به يوما وما هو من الظالمين ببعيد

TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r2.claim: The clause is circumstantial and كم is an exclamatory report, not a question: many earlier peoples had better furnishings and appearances yet were destroyed.
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن الجملة حالية وكم خبرية لا استفهامية، والمعنى أنهم يتفوهون بهذه الشبهة الواهية

TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r3.claim: The boast recalls Pharaoh, who cited his Egyptian kingdom and rivers to claim superiority, then was drowned and made an example for later peoples.
TABATABAI:19:74-75#2/r3.anchor: وقد نقل سبحانه نظير هذه الشبهة عن فرعون وعقبه بحديث غرقه وهلاكه

TABRISI:19:71/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:71/r4.claim: Athāth means decorative household goods and clothes; some say it has no singular, others give athātha.
TABRISI:19:71/r4.anchor: والأثاث المتاع من الفرش والثياب التي تزين بها واحدها أثاثة

TABRISI:19:71/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:71/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:71/r5.claim: Riy is outward appearance and names the thing seen, like the noun for slaughtered meat.
TABRISI:19:71/r5.anchor: والري ما يراه الرجل من ظاهر أحوال القوم وهو اسم للمرئي

TABRISI:19:72-75/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:72-75/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:72-75/r5.claim: Athāth means possessions and decoration, riy means appearance; earlier nations had more of both and were still destroyed.
TABRISI:19:72-75/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس الأثاث المتاع وزينة الدنيا والرءي المنظر والهيئة

TABRISI:19:72-75/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:72-75/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:72-75/r6.claim: Earlier nations' wealth and beauty did not save them, so present wealth and beauty will not save these people either.
TABRISI:19:72-75/r6.anchor: فأهلك أموالهم وأفسد عليهم صورهم ولم تغن عنهم أموالهم ولا جمالهم

TABRISI:19:72-75/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:72-75/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:72-75/r7.claim: Another identification is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and his associates, who groomed their hair, wore silk, and boasted of their appearance.
TABRISI:19:72-75/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن المعني بالآية النضر بن الحارث وذووه وكانوا يرجلون شعورهم

THALABI:v6p228/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p228/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p228/r6.claim: God answers that earlier generations He destroyed possessed better furnishings and goods.
THALABI:v6p228/r6.anchor: مجيبا لهم وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا أي متاعا

THALABI:v6p228/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p228/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p228/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains athāthan as appearance or bearing; Muqatil calls it clothing.
THALABI:v6p228/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هيئة وقال مقاتل: ثيابا

THALABI:v6p228/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p228/r8.speaker: أبي
THALABI:v6p228/r8.claim: Ubay reads ziyan instead of riʾyan, meaning appearance or attire.
THALABI:v6p228/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبي: وزيا بالزاي وهو الهيئة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r1.claim: Athāth means kinds of household possessions and furnishings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r1.anchor: قال الليث: (الأثاث: أنواع المتاع من متاع البيت ونحوه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r2.claim: Athāth means all property, including livestock, slaves, and household goods; its singular is athātha.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r2.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: (الأثاث: المال أجمع، المال، والإبل، والغنم، والعبيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r3.claim: Athāth has no singular, like matāʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: (الأثاث: لا واحد له، كما أن المتاع لا واحد له)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r8.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r8.claim: Better furnishings means rugs and carpets.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r8.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله: {أحسن أثاثا} قال: (مثل # الدرانيك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r9.claim: The root describes a plant growing thick and intertwined, and also describes dense hair; the cited poem uses athīth for such hair.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p303/r9.anchor: وأصل الحرف من قولهم: أث النبات يئث أثاثة إذا كثر والتف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:74-75/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:74-75/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:74-75/r1.claim: Earlier generations had better furnishings and appearance than these disbelievers, but that did not avail them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:74-75/r1.anchor: وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا } متاعا { ورئيا } منظرا من هؤلاء الكفار، فلم يغن ذلك عنهم شيئا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r7.claim: Earlier generations destroyed by God had more furnishings and a finer outward appearance than the current claimants.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r7.anchor: قال الله: {وكم أهلكنا قبلهم من قرن هم أحسن أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] منهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r8.claim: Athāth means wealth; another view takes it as household goods or possessions.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r9.claim: With the hamzated reading, ruʾyan means appearance; Qatāda glosses it as more goods and a better look, while al-Hasan says forms or images.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r9.anchor: {ورئيا} [مريم: 74] من قرأها مهموزة فيقول: منظرا. سعيد، عن قتادة قال: {أحسن أثاثا ورئيا} [مريم: 74] أكثر متاعا وأحسن مرآة ومنظرا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r10.claim: Without hamza, the word derives from good appearance; people's livelihood depends on rain, which grows crops and sustains livestock.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p239/r10.anchor: ومن قرأها بغير همزة فيقول: وريا من قبل الرواء. وإنما عيش الناس بالمطر

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r4.claim: The verse recalls prosperous peoples such as ʿĀd and Thamūd, who cultivated land and built thriving countries but were destroyed for disbelief, urging the arrogant to learn from their remains.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:73/r4.anchor: Âd ve Semûd gibi eski kavimlerin akıbetleri hatırlatılarak onların kalıntılarına bakıp ibret almaları tavsiye edilmektedir

SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r1.claim: كم is obligatorily fronted as an interrogative or exclamative; here it is exclamative, and من قرن specifies it.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r1.anchor: قوله: { وكم أهلكنا }: " كم " مفعول مقدم واجب التقديم؛

SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r2.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r2.claim: They treat هم أحسن as an accusative adjective of كم, reasoning that without هم the comparative would be accusative as an adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r2.anchor: أنها في محل نصب، صفة ل " كم ". قال الزمخشري: " ألا ترى أنك لو أسقطت " هم "

SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r3.claim: That analysis conflicts with the rule that كم, whether interrogative or exclamative, is neither qualified nor qualifying.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r3.anchor: وفي هذا نظر لأن النحويين نصوا: على أن " كم " استفهامية كانت أو خبرية لا توصف

SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r4.claim: هم أحسن is instead a genitive adjective of قرن; its plural pronoun matches قرن's collective sense, as with جميع used with singular or plural agreement.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r4.anchor: الثاني: أنها في محل جر صفة ل " قرن " ولا محذور في هذا، وإنما جمع في قوله: " هم "

SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r5.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r5.claim: The common reading is رئيا with silent hamza then yāʾ; Hamza changes hamza to yāʾ at pause, with either clear articulation or assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r5.anchor: قوله: " ورئيا " الجمهور على " رئيا " الجمهور على " رئيا " بهمزة ساكنة بعدها ياء صريحة وصلا ووفقا،

SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r6.claim: Assimilation at pause can confuse the word with الري, fullness and freshness; Abu ʿAmr therefore avoids his usual hamza easing here.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r6.anchor: وفي الإدغام إبهام أنها مادة أخرى: وهو الري الذي بمعنى الامتلاء والنضارة،

SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r7.speaker: قالون وابن ذكوان
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r7.claim: They read وريا with doubled yāʾ, explained either from an original hamza replaced and assimilated, or as beauty/fullness.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74/r7.anchor: وقرأ قالون عن نافع، وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر " وريا " بياء مشددة بعد الراء،

SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r1.speaker: حميد وأبو بكر بن عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r1.claim: They read وريئا with silent yāʾ followed by hamza, a metathesis of رئيا; the cited poem witnesses راءني.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ حميد وأبو بكر بن عاصم في رواية الأعشى " وريئا " بياء ساكنة بعدها همزة

SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r2.claim: The reading is explained as reversed from the common form and derived from راءه يراه; the author doubts the metathesis.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r2.anchor: وهو مقلوب من " رئيا " في قراءة العامة، ووزنه فلع، وهو من راءه يرآه

SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r3.claim: The author calls the proposed metathesis doubtful.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r3.anchor: وفي القلب من القلب ما فيه.

SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r4.speaker: اليزيدي
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r4.claim: Al-Yazidi transmits ورياء, from showing off; the first hamza is regularly softened to yāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r4.anchor: وروى اليزيدي قراءة " ورياء " بياء بعدها ألف، بعدها همزة، وهي من المراءاة،

SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r5.claim: In Talha's narration, Ibn ʿAbbas reads وريا lightly; one derivation deletes the second yāʾ from the doubled form to ease its weight.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس أيضا في رواية طلحة " وريا " بياء فقط مخففة.

SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r6.claim: The light-yāʾ form may also derive from وريئا by moving hamza's vowel to the prior yāʾ and deleting hamza; those who call it erroneous missed this analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون أصلها كقراءة حميد " وريئا " بالقلب، ثم نقل حركة الهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r7.claim: They and others read وزيا with zāy and doubled yāʾ, meaning fine dress and collected ornaments, from زوى, to gather.
SAMIN-DURR:19:74#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس أيضا وابن جبير وجماعة " وزيا " بزاي وياء مشددة،

ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r4.claim: Three readings are cited—رئيا, ريا, and زيا—and a fourth, ريئا, is linguistically possible but not reported as a reading.
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r4.anchor: فيها أربعة أوجه رئيا بهمزة قبل الياء

ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r5.claim: رئيا means fine appearance beside furnishings; unhamzated ريا either drops the hamza with the same sense or suggests luxuriance visibly expressed in their appearance.
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r5.anchor: فالمعنى فيه هم أحسن أثاثا أي متاعا

ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r6.claim: زيا means good attire or appearance; the accusative phrase explains how the destroyed generations surpassed their successors.
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r6.anchor: ومن قرأ زيا فمعناه أن زيهم حسن يعني هيئتهم

ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r7.claim: ريئا is a metathesized form of رئيا; the verse by the poet Kathīr attests the alternate expression راءني for رآني.
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ ريئا فهو بمعنى رئيا مقلوب لأن من العرب من يقول قد راءني زيد

ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r8.speaker: كثير
ZAJJAJ:v3p341/r8.claim: Kathīr's poem uses راءني as the form whose inversion supports the variant ريئا.

ASAD-NOTES:19:74#n60/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:74#n60/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:74#n60/r1.claim: Qarn here means people of one epoch, or a civilization, while the property term means abundance of wealth.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r2.claim: Both pronunciations of مقام are place nouns, not action nouns; the following comparison of furnishings and appearance supports a residence sense.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p208/r2.anchor: فأما المقام فيمن ضم، وفيمن فتح على اسم المكان، وليس اسم الحدث،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r1.claim: Most readers hamzate رئيا between rāʾ and yāʾ; Ibn Amir and Nafi often omit hamza, though several transmissions from both preserve it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: ورئيا مهموزة بين الراء والياء في وزن رعيا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda defines الرئي as what appears outwardly to the eye.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r2.anchor: أبو عبيدة: رئيا ما ظهر مما رأيت .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r3.claim: رئي is a noun for what is seen, not the verbal noun; the source distinguishes it from الرأي and الرؤية and compares parallel patterns.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: رئي فعل من رأيت، وكأنه اسم لما ظهر وليس المصدر،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r4.claim: The Asim form وريئا shifts the hamza to the word's end; رواء may derive from seeing with softened hamza or from fullness, meaning freshness and radiance.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r4.anchor: فأما ما روي عن عاصم من قوله: (وريئا)، فإنه قلب الهمزة التي هي عين إلى موضع اللام

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r5.claim: Softening hamza in رئيا yields yāʾ because of the preceding kasra and then assimilation; another transmission drops it and transfers its vowel to the preceding yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p209#2/r5.anchor: ومن خفف الهمزة من رئيا لزم أن يبدل منها الياء لانكسار ما قبلها كما تبدل من ذيب وبير،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p42/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p42/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p42/r4.claim: Ṭalḥa reads وريّا without hamza; Saʿīd b. Jubayr, Yazīd al-Barbarī, and al-Aʿṣam al-Makkī read وزيا. وريّا may derive from رؤية with hamza lightened and assimilated, or from روِيَ, ‘fresh and handsome.’
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p42/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة طلحة: "وريا"5، خفيفة بلا همز. وقرأ: "وزيا"، [97ظ] بالزاي سعيد بن جبير ويزيد البربري والأعسم المكي

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p44/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p44/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p44/r1.claim: The unhamzated riyāʾ may come from رئيا with hamza deleted and its vowel shifted, or from روِيَ with one of the doubled yāʾs deleted, usually the second weak final letter.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p44/r1.anchor: فأما "ريا"، مخففة غير مهموزة فتحتمل أمرين:

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p44/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p44/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p44/r2.claim: The zāy reading زِيّ derives from زويت, ‘I gathered’: the adornments are plentiful; the Prophet's ‘زويت لي الأرض’ and al-Aʿshā's poetry support the root.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p44/r2.anchor: وأما "الزي"، بالزاي ففعل من زويت؛ وذلك أنه لا يقال لمن له شيء واحد من آلته: زي1

IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r3.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī hamzate warʾiyā; Ibn ʿĀmir omits hamza. Nāfiʿ transmissions differ, with some hamzating and others omitting it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r3.anchor: 19 واختلفوا فى الهمز وتركه من قوله ﴿ ورئيا ﴾ 74

QIRAAT-ER:19:74:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:74:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:74:10#1/r1.claim: The standard reading retains hamza in riʾyan, forming a glottal break in the noun for outward appearance.
QIRAAT-ER:19:74:10#1/r1.anchor: Standard canonical reading; hamza retained creating glottal break; root r-ʾ-y; noun riʾy = outward appearance

QIRAAT-ER:19:74:10#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:74:10#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:74:10#2/r1.claim: The second canonical reading drops hamza and doubles yāʾ by assimilation, with the same root and meaning but smoother phonology.
QIRAAT-ER:19:74:10#2/r1.anchor: Hamza dropped, yāʾ doubled by assimilation; same root and meaning; second 7-canonical reading

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p11#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p11#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p11#2/r1.claim: Qatada explains the earlier peoples' greater furnishing and appearance as greater wealth and more attractive forms.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p11#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أحسن أثاثا ورئيا ﴾ قال أكثر أموالا وأحسن صورا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r1.speaker: أبو بكر عن الأعمش عن عاصم، حميد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r1.claim: They read ورءيا with a quiescent ra followed by ya and hamza, using metathesis from راء; a poetic line is cited as evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر في رواية الأعمش عن عاصم وحميد ورءيا بياء ساكنة بعدها همزة وهو على القلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r2.speaker: اليزيدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r2.claim: Al-Yazidi transmits ورياء with ya, alif, and hamza, from showing off: people display their beauty to one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r2.anchor: وقرىء ورياء بياء بعدها ألف بعدها همزة، حكاها اليزيدي وأصله ورئاء من المراءاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r3.speaker: ابن عباس فيما روى عنه طلحة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to read ريا without hamza or doubling; Abu Hayyan rejects calling it erroneous and derives it from good appearance by metathesis or luxuriant growth with a deleted ya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس، فيما روى عنه طلحة وريا من غير همز ولا تشديد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، يزيد البربري، الأعسم المكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r4.claim: They read زيا with a doubled ya and zay, meaning fine adornment and pleasingly assembled possessions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p291/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس أيضا وابن جبير ويزيد البربري والأعسم المكي وزيا بالزاي مشدد الياء وهي البزة الحسنة،

ITQAN:v2p349/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p349/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p349/r5.claim: أثاث is furnishings or possessions, while رئي is glossed as drink; a poetic line cites the expression الرئي الكريم من الأثاث.
ITQAN:v2p349/r5.anchor: قال الأثاث المتاع والرئي من الشراب قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت الشاعر يقول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r3.claim: The interpretation of ri'yan as drink, from reyy or satiation, is not one of the seven canonical readings; she rejects it because the hamzated form retains the sense of seeing.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r3.anchor: وتفسير "رئى" بأنه: من الشراب، كأنه أُخِذ من الرَّىَّ، وليست قراءة الأئمة السبعة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r4.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r4.claim: Tabari says the majority read ri'yan from visual sight, as an active form used with passive meaning, like grinding or watering; Ibn Abbas glosses it as appearance, or good appearance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r4.anchor: وفيها قال الطبري: وقرأ الجمهور "ورئيا" من رؤية العين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ri'yan as outward appearance, with a second report specifying a pleasing appearance.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p329/r5.anchor: ثم أسند عن ابن عباس قال: الرئى المنظر. وفي رواية عنه: المنظر الحسن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r1.claim: The answer in the Ibn al-Azraq question exchange glosses athāthan as possessions and raʾyan as drink, adducing a poetic line as evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r1.anchor: قال: الأثاث المتاع، والرئى الشراب. واستشهد بقول الشاعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r2.claim: Bukhari and al-Tabari report Ibn Abbas’s gloss of athāth as mataʿ, worldly goods.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r2.anchor: تفسير الأثاث في المسألة بالمتاع، أخرجه البخاري في كتاب التفسير عن ابن عباس وأسنده الطبري عنه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r3.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ says athāth means possessions and has no singular form, though the word can be pluralized.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء في معنى الآية: الأثاث المتاع، لا واحد لهما، وقد يجمعان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r4.speaker: الأزهري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r4.claim: Al-Azhari restricts athāth to household furnishings.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r5.speaker: الهروي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r5.claim: Al-Harawi’s al-Gharībayn restricts athāth to things worn and spread out.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r5.anchor: وخصه الهروى في (الغريبين) بما يلبس ويفترش

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r6.claim: From Quranic usage, the author finds athāth usually denotes abundant household furnishings and rarely abstract things, while mataʿ broadly covers worldly goods.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p328/r6.anchor: الأثاث يستعمل، أكثر ما يستعمل، في متاع البيت بخاصة، ومع ملحظ الوفرة والكثرة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p330/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p330/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p330/r1.claim: The author distinguishes seeing through the senses, thought or intellect, and what is seen in dreams; raʾy may be witnessed or imagined.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p330/r1.anchor: بالحاسة، أو الرأى بالفكر والعقل، والرؤيا لما يُرى في المنام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p330/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p330/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p330/r2.claim: The author rejects the gloss ‘drink’ as unsupported by Arabic usage and prefers a visible or imagined scene or appearance; the cited poem is better read this way too.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p330/r2.anchor: فيقرُب أن يكون: مشهداًَ، ومنظرا يُرى بالعين أو يُتخيل على الوهم والظن والفتنة

NASHR:v1p471/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r1.speaker: صاحب الكافي وصاحب التبصرة
NASHR:v1p471/r1.claim: For hamza in tuʾwīhi and ruʾyan, al-Kāfī and al-Tabṣira prefer replacing it with a matching wāw or yāʾ without assimilation; al-Tabṣira says this is the established practice.
NASHR:v1p471/r1.anchor: ورجح الإظهار صاحب " الكافي "، وصاحب " التبصرة " وقال: إنه الذي عليه العمل

NASHR:v1p471/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r2.speaker: صاحب التذكرة والداني
NASHR:v1p471/r2.claim: Al-Tadhkira and al-Dānī prefer replacement followed by assimilation, citing its explicit transmission from Hamza and agreement with the rasm; al-ʿUnwān likewise gives only this form.
NASHR:v1p471/r2.anchor: ورجح الإدغام صاحب " التذكرة " والداني في " جامع البيان " فقال: هو أولى ; لأنه قد جاء منصوصا عن حمزة، ولموافقة الرسم

NASHR:v1p471/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r3.speaker: صاحب التيسير
NASHR:v1p471/r3.claim: Al-Taysīr gives the two treatments equally, and al-Shāṭibī follows that presentation.
NASHR:v1p471/r3.anchor: وأطلق صاحب " التيسير " الوجهين على السواء، وتبعه على ذلك الشاطبي

NASHR:v1p471/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p471/r4.claim: Al-Tadhkira adds full hamza realization in ruʾyan to avoid a meaning change, but the author rejects it for contradicting transmitted reading and performance.
NASHR:v1p471/r4.anchor: وزاد في " التذكرة " في (رءيا) ، وجها ثالثا، وهو التحقيق من أجل تغيير المعنى، ولا يؤخذ به؛ لمخالفته النص والأداء

NASHR:v1p471/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r5.speaker: الفارسي
NASHR:v1p471/r5.claim: Al-Fārisī reports a fourth option, deleting hamza and stopping with one light yāʾ according to the rasm; the author says it is invalid and forbidden.
NASHR:v1p471/r5.anchor: وحكى الفارسي وجها رابعا، وهو الحذف، أي: حذف الهمزة فيوقف بياء واحدة مخففة

NASHR:v1p471/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p471/r6.claim: For ruʾyā wherever it occurs, readers agree to replace the quiescent hamza with wāw after ḍamma.
NASHR:v1p471/r6.anchor: فأجمعوا على إبدال الهمزة منه واوا لسكونها وضم ما قبلها

NASHR:v1p471/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r7.speaker: الهذلي
NASHR:v1p471/r7.claim: Al-Hudhali, al-Dānī, and others allow Abū Jaʿfar's assimilation of the wāw into the following yāʾ; Ibn Shurayḥ also reports it but weakens it.
NASHR:v1p471/r7.anchor: فأجازه أبو القاسم الهذلي، والحافظ أبو عمرو، وغيرهما، وسووا بينه وبين الإظهار

NASHR:v1p471/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p471/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p471/r8.claim: Although assimilation agrees with the rasm, the author prefers clear articulation as more analogical and the practice of most reciters; deletion based only on rasm is impermissible.
NASHR:v1p471/r8.anchor: فإن الإظهار أولى وأقيس، وعليه أكثر أهل الأداء، وحكي فيه وجه ثالث
